facts.fact: The Minister for Communications and Digitalisation says the eGovernment network (GovNet) connects government agencies including MMDAs by fibre backbone, last-mile fibre and microwave links with VSAT backup, provided to the institutions on a 10-year indefeasible right of use, with 274 of 274 MMDA sites connected.
facts.system: eGovernment Network Connectivity Infrastructure (eGovNet / GovNet, DSIG 100x)

facts.fact: The minister's table of sites connected by the eGovNet gives MMDAs 274 of 274 planned sites, within 950 of 951 government sites in all; she says the sites were chosen by the beneficiary institutions and that Ghana has 261 districts, and does not say how many of the 261 assemblies the 274 sites cover.
facts.system: eGovernment Network Connectivity Infrastructure (eGovNet / GovNet, DSIG 100x)

facts.fact: The minister says the network gives the connected agencies, MMDAs among them, faster communication and access to government shared services and lets them use digital solutions; she names no system that assembly staff work in over it.
facts.system: eGovernment Network Connectivity Infrastructure (eGovNet / GovNet, DSIG 100x)

facts.fact: The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation tendered the eGovNet in September 2021 under a 10-year contract, awarded it to AirtelTigo and Ascend Digital Solutions in September 2022 and signed in December 2022; the minister calls it government-owned infrastructure.
facts.system: eGovernment Network Connectivity Infrastructure (eGovNet / GovNet, DSIG 100x)

facts.fact: The minister says the eGovNet bidding was supervised by the World Bank project implementation team but gives no cost and names no source of funds for the network.
facts.system: eGovernment Network Connectivity Infrastructure (eGovNet / GovNet, DSIG 100x)

facts.fact: The minister says the eGovNet was 95% complete at the end of January 2024, a little over a year after the contract was signed in December 2022, and was expected to be fully complete by the end of February 2024.
facts.system: eGovernment Network Connectivity Infrastructure (eGovNet / GovNet, DSIG 100x)

systems.country_label: eGovNet; GovNet; Digital Super Information Gateway (DSIG 100x)
systems.platform: 100 Gbps fibre backbone, over 5,000 km of fibre, 900 microwave links, 800 VSAT terminals as backup, SD-WAN overlay
systems.owner: Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation; built under a 10-year contract by AirtelTigo and Ascend Digital Solutions
systems.tiers: 951 planned government sites nationwide: MMDAs 274, police 255 of 256, post offices 175, health facilities 97, GIFMIS institutions 79, courts 36, GMET 29, NITA 3, universities 2

systems.platform: Online services and payments platform built and run by a consortium of Hubtel, expressPay and IT Consortium
systems.owner: Government of Ghana, under a public-private partnership with the consortium
systems.tiers: Shared point for government online revenue collection; 261 MMDAs onboarded from 2022 (32 in 2020 and 2021), within 1,507 institutions onboarded, of which 136 were processing live payments in January 2024

systems.country_label: e-Services Platform; Ghana E-Services Payment Platform (GEPP)
systems.platform: Portal by IPMC (2012) with a Magento payment platform by AYA Technologies (2014)
systems.tiers: AMA onboarded in 2014 for notice of marriage and marriage registration, among five active agencies; discontinued

systems.system: e-Government network managed by NITA and SmartInfraco
systems.tiers: Not stated; to be interconnected with the eGovNet
